neighbours.label: a negating or limiting word after a modal or clause boundary (will not, but even, little more than)
fire: The new rules may not significantly reduce the number of accidents.
Rooftop panels would be ideal, but even in cloudy regions they help.
Without rain there won't be enough water for the crops this summer.
Such claims may be rooted in little more than wishful thinking.
Satisfying every request will not be possible with this budget.
The repair should not take longer than a single afternoon.
Prices rose sharply, but few buyers seemed to notice.
The treaty might not survive another change of government.
quiet: The new rules may significantly reduce the number of accidents.
Rooftop panels would be ideal, and in sunny regions they help a lot.
With rain there will be enough water for the crops this summer.
Such claims may be rooted in careful study of the evidence.
Satisfying every request will be possible with this budget.
The repair should take about a single afternoon.
Prices rose sharply, and many buyers seemed to notice.
The treaty might survive another change of government.
